layers.note: A scattered understory tree beneath old conifer forest, often near streams.

moisture.note: Moist ground: stream terraces, ravines and lower slopes.

heat_load.note: Favours cool, shaded aspects and ravines; scarce on hot south-west slopes.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,200 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: Grows on slopes and in ravines.

shade_tolerance.note: Extremely shade tolerant: lives its whole life under the canopy.

sun_tolerance.note: Yew left in the open after logging declines, its foliage yellowed and scorched.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −7 °C, gone by −12 °C, up to about 10 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −28 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −36 °C.

warmest_c.note: Warmest-month means from about 12.5 to 24 °C; gone below 10 °C, where summers are too short, and above 28 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,800 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,100.

degree_days_5.note: About 800 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 400: from the lowlands to the montane forest.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.55, gone by 0.4.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit; its range takes in summer-dry coasts and interior mountains with some summer rain, to about 0.45 of the year's precipitation.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Pacific yew grows in the understory from south-east Alaska to central California and inland to Idaho and Montana (Silvics of North America, vol. 1). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
